doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Louis and Joe Glaser
summary: Louis' priorities were his horn, Glaser and Lucille; Glaser made deals for other acts.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well with Louis. And he was pretty much controlled or under the thumb of Joe Glaser? Is that right? Or was he his own man?

No he was his own man. No Louis used to say, I heard him say on many occasions, especially if he had a couple of beers, he’d say “three things in my life that matter to me: my horn, Joe Glaser and Lucille.” And not necessarily in that order. I don’t remember how he said it, but those are the things he thought about, that he cared about. Everything else, forget about it, I don’t care. But people would say Louis made Joe Glaser rich. And © Fillius Jazz Archive -26-

I say yeah, well Joe Glaser made Louie rich, too, because Joe Glaser would make some kind of deals with promoters, he’d say “you want Louis? You’ve got to book Red Norvo,” or you’ve got to take so-and-so. He would make deals for different people. He was a sharp, smart promoter.
So some of the other musicians profited from that association too.
Well Red Norvo was getting more work because of Louis.
